proposals.evidence: Turner gives Gujarati kādav mud under kardama, beside Middle Indo-Aryan kaddama and Hindi kādaw. These Bhili-area forms preserve the diagnostic intervocalic v or its vocalic trace before a diminutive ḍ suffix. The kād- family comparison is secure at this level; expressive suffix and occasional aspiration are qualifications, and bare eastern kāda forms are excluded because karda competes.

proposals.evidence: Turner’s seventh *bhuṇḍa branch explicitly includes Gujarati bhũḍũ bad and Hindi bhū̃ḍā ugly. The Bhili survey nasal-retroflex-ḍ forms fit this Gujarati-border bad adjective family, with local endings preserved. The ṭ form and northern Punjabi-like bhuṇḍā forms are excluded because Turner assigns competing branches there.
